title: Chinese slurs, cooperative businesses and neighborhood ties
summary: He explains the slur "ha quay", the reserved Chinese cooperative businesses, and how they depended on black neighborhoods.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up under segregation: schools, neighborhoods, Jim Crow

blocks.x: I see. OK. Were there any words that the Chinese used that offended Afro-Cubans? Do you know of any?
'Ha Quay' means the equivalent of nigger.
I see; and was that used a lot?

But naturally, you don't know the meaning or the way they used it not until you find out somebody, because they very reserved, they very reserved, they won't tell you anything. As a matter of fact, we used to get into a restaurant or a place that sells fruit, a fruit store, and you were talking with the owner and they say "No, the captain is not here, the owner is not here", so you never know who was the owner of the place because they work in cooperatives like the, what you call it, the this nationality that comes from Grecia, the Greeks. They get together four or five guys, they chip in a thousand or five hundred dollars and they open a restaurant and nobody is the owner. / That's why they are so succesful.
That's why they don't hire nobody else, because they work among them.
I see. Okay. As far as you can remember, were they very discriminatory or just only against Afro-Cubans?

Yeah, but - they was kind of careful because we don't use to take nothing from nobody, we used to fight any moment, so on account that they were discriminated by the other group so they were in the middle.
You mean the white Cubans discriminated against them also.
Right, so they was in the middle so they get together with us more because all the business that they had was in the neighborhood.
After they got into - up and they opened this chic places like Macy's or Korvettes or whatever.
